name: saved Huntersville textarea beats generic Yes

Important: You must be legally authorized to work in the Country for any location you select. Relocation assistance, if available, will be discussed during the recruiting process.

spec_quote: When the field is a free TEXT box with no options and a saved text answer exists for that very question, the saved text answer is used.

name: saved shift answer used when no rule answers

args.label: What is your preferred shift?

spec_quote: A question that no rule answers gets its saved answer ("What is your preferred shift?" → "Day shift").

name: generic Yes on free-text relocation explanation box asks

args.label: Are you willing to relocate? If yes, please describe your location preferences.

spec_quote: A question with no saved answer keeps the rules' behaviour (a Yes / No on a text box that is not a yes/no question → ask).

name: radio Yes-No work authorization keeps rule Yes

args.label: Are you legally authorized to work in the United States?

spec_quote: A radio / select question with Yes / No options still gets the rule's Yes / No (a Yes / No fits there).

name: saved Huntersville answer on location-ranking variant

args.label: This position is available in Huntersville, NC (USA); Brampton, ON (CAN). Please rank your preferred work locations in order of interest.

spec_quote: Q1: the question containing both "rank your preferred work locations" and "Huntersville" → text "Huntersville, NC (USA)".

name: three professional references asks

spec_quote: A question that asks for references / referees (their names, companies, positions, phone numbers, e-mail addresses — "Enter three professional references …", "Reference 1 – Email", "Please list two referees") is never answered with any of the candidate's own facts

name: reference-checks consent is not a references question

args.label: I acknowledge and consent to reference checks as part of the hiring process.

spec_quote: A sentence that only mentions "reference checks" as part of the hiring process (a consent / acknowledgement box) … is NOT a references question (it keeps whatever the other rules do, and must never be "ask" because of references).

name: with reference to is not a references question

args.label: With reference to the job requirements, are you legally authorized to work in the United States?

spec_quote: or "with reference to …" is NOT a references question (it keeps whatever the other rules do, and must never be "ask" because of references).

name: OPT as example in authorization question is Yes

args.label: Are you legally authorized to work in the United States (e.g., U.S. citizen, permanent resident, F-1 OPT)?

spec_quote: "Are you legally authorized to work in the United States (e.g., U.S. citizen, permanent resident, F-1 OPT)?" — OPT / CPT appear only as examples of authorization → it is the work-authorization question → **Yes**.

name: OPT etc parenthetical in authorization question is Yes

args.label: Are you legally authorized to work in the United States? (U.S. citizen, green card holder, OPT, etc.)

spec_quote: Parenthesised example lists ("(U.S. citizen, green card holder, OPT, etc.)", "(such as OPT or CPT)") count as examples too.

name: currently on OPT is not answered Yes

args.label: Are you currently on OPT?

spec_quote: A question that asks whether he is ON OPT ("Are you currently authorized to work on OPT?", "Are you currently on OPT?") is not answered Yes by this rule (he is not on OPT: No, or ask).
ambiguous_reason: The spec allows either No or ask for an on-OPT question, so the expected outcome cannot be a single exact value.

name: work without sponsorship now only is Yes

args.label: Are you legally able to work in the U.S. without sponsorship? (e.g., OPT, CPT)

spec_quote: Work WITHOUT sponsorship: "Are you legally able to work in the U.S. without sponsorship? (e.g., OPT, CPT)" — the sponsorship answer flipped: the question covers only now / this internship → **Yes**

name: work without sponsorship now or future is No

args.label: Are you legally able to work in the U.S. without sponsorship now or in the future?

spec_quote: when it also covers the future ("now or in the future", "at any time", "after graduation") → **No**.

name: such as OPT or CPT parenthetical is Yes

args.label: Are you authorized to work in the United States? (such as OPT or CPT)

spec_quote: Parenthesised example lists ("(U.S. citizen, green card holder, OPT, etc.)", "(such as OPT or CPT)") count as examples too.

name: currently pursuing degree and major

args.label: Please include what degree you are currently pursuing in addition to major(s) and any minor(s).

spec_quote: "Please include what degree you are currently pursuing in addition to major(s) and any minor(s)." → **"M.S. Applied Data Science"** (degree and major together, from his education; nothing about a minor is added).

name: completed bachelor degree and major

args.label: What degree and major did you complete for your bachelor's degree?

spec_quote: A degree + major question about the completed / highest / undergraduate (bachelor's) degree → "B.A. Economics".

name: plain degree and major text box

args.label: Degree and major

spec_quote: A plain "Degree and major" text box (no tense) → the current program "M.S. Applied Data Science".

name: degree major and graduation date asks

args.label: Degree, major and expected graduation date

spec_quote: or a box that also asks a date / GPA / school name ("Degree, major and expected graduation date") → ask.

name: degree and major with options asks

args.label: Degree and major

spec_quote: The same box with options, or a box that also asks a date / GPA / school name ("Degree, major and expected graduation date") → ask.

name: major-only question keeps major answer

args.label: What is your major?

spec_quote: A question about only the degree, or only the major, keeps its own answers (degree → "Master's Degree", major → "Data Science").

name: combined Data Science slash Analytics option wins

args.label: Please select your major / field of study.

spec_quote: A major / field-of-study list whose options combine fields with "/", "&", "," or "and" ("Data Science / Analytics", "Applied Data Science / Economics", "Statistics and Data Science") is matched by the parts of each option, in the preference order: the option holding the earliest preferred field wins, before any later field and before "Other".

name: whole Data Science option beats combined same-field option

args.label: Major / field of study

spec_quote: A whole option that equals a preferred field wins over a combined option that holds only the same or a later field ("Data Science" over "Statistics and Data Science").

name: combined Applied Data Science option beats later Data Analytics

args.label: Select your field of study

spec_quote: the option holding the earliest preferred field wins, before any later field and before "Other".

name: combined Statistics and Data Science holds earliest Data Science part

args.label: Select your major

spec_quote: is matched by the parts of each option, in the preference order: the option holding the earliest preferred field wins, before any later field and before "Other".

name: no preferred field anywhere gives Other

args.label: Field of study

spec_quote: A list with no preferred field anywhere → "Other" when offered.
